title: What Is a Permanent Stamp Worth in Canada?
description: A Permanent stamp is worth $1.24, mails a letter up to 30 g anywhere in Canada, and stays valid at the current domestic rate after any price rise.
answer: A Canadian Permanent stamp has a postage value of $1.24. It carries no printed amount and always pays for a standard letter up to 30 grams anywhere in Canada. Canada Post accepts it at the current domestic rate even after prices rise, so a Permanent stamp bought today stays usable.

blocks.p: Canada Post describes the Permanent stamp as a non-denominated stamp with a postage value of $1.24. One stamp mails a letter weighing up to 30 g anywhere in Canada.

Canada Post's stamp page says a Permanent stamp is always accepted at the current domestic postage rate and can be used at any time, now or in the future, even if rates have increased. A rate rise changes what a new stamp costs, not what an old Permanent stamp is worth.
If the domestic rate rises, a Permanent stamp bought at $1.24 still pays for a standard letter. That is a property of the stamp, not a forecast, and it applies only to the up-to-30 g domestic letter.

sections.h2: Using a Permanent stamp for heavier mail

blocks.p: Canada Post says Permanent stamps can be combined with additional postage to mail larger letters or parcels, or to send mail internationally. For a domestic letter, count stamps by weight: [how many stamps a letter needs](/blog/how-many-stamps-for-a-letter-in-canada).

sections.h2: Why it matters to a mailing service

blocks.p: sendletter stamps letters with Permanent coil stamps and charges exactly their value, $1.24 each, with no postage margin.

sources.label: Canada Post, What are Permanent stamps?
